page: Microsoft Azure L32s_v4 is an Lsv4-family virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 32 vCPUs, 16 physical cores, and a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture CPU includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB per core, and includes 7679 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance in memory bandwidth, with large-block read-only operations reaching 197.62 GB/sec. The server demonstrates top-tier performance in image processing with a Geekbench score of 18415.0 and small-model LLM text generation at 392.66 tokens/sec. Single-threaded gzip compression and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression are also strong. However, text generation for large 70B LLM models is a notable performance bottleneck, registering a weak score of 2.78 tokens/sec.

The L32s_v4 offers high resource density by combining a high-frequency CPU with a substantial local NVMe SSD storage capacity and a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. This configuration provides qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require high-speed local scratch space and large memory footprints without the overhead of external storage. It is highly suited for large-scale databases, data warehousing, big data analytics, and memory-intensive applications that benefit from rapid local storage I/O.
